I read garnet's default calibration (set f81c45da-6e73-4b5d-a0fe-72c75635fade). I checked every connected chain of 3 qubits, meaning a middle qubit with two CZ neighbours. The best chain is QB11-QB12-QB7. The two IRB CZ fidelities are 0.99869 (QB12-QB11) and 0.99802 (QB12-QB7). Their product is 0.99671. The next best chain, QB16-QB11-QB12, scores about 0.9947.

I built a 3-qubit GHZ circuit. It puts a Hadamard on the middle qubit QB12, then uses CZ gates only on QB12-QB11 and QB12-QB7. Each CZ is sandwiched between Hadamards on the target qubit to make a CNOT. I transpiled it with that layout and the compiled circuit has exactly 2 CZ gates. I ran it on garnet:mock with 200 shots and measured all 3 qubits.

Final job counts, in Qiskit bit order with QB11 as the rightmost bit: 001:58, 000:51, 110:48, 111:43. These are not a clean GHZ result, because a perfect run would give only 000 and 111. The mock does not simulate the circuit and returns random counts, so the counts do not show real noise. A real run would show mostly 000 and 111, with the leftover counts caused by the roughly 0.3 percent CZ error on each pair plus readout error.

I ran the script 3 times by mistake, because I appended debug lines and re-ran it. All three jobs were on the free mock, at 0 credits. The first job ID is 01a16042-4b6b-70dd-a40a-2056c5b403f9. The second job ID was not captured, because its output was cut off by a tail. The third and final job ID is 01a16042-c243-73f4-a235-0df93fede5a8. The chain is QB11-QB12-QB7, with QB12 as the middle qubit.
